simple.meaning: גָּזַל (gâzal) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to pluck off ; specifically to flay , strip or rob.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 30 times across Genesis, Leviticus, Deuteronomy, Judges, 2 Samuel, and 9 more, beginning at Genesis 21:25. Its contexts include family line, mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גָּזַל (H1497).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: גָּזַל (gâzal) / H1497 is traced through Genesis 21:25, Genesis 31:31, Leviticus 5:23, Leviticus 19:13 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: Abraham complained to Abimelech because of a water well, which Abimelech’s servants had violently taken away.
Jacob answered Laban, “Because I was afraid, for I said, ‘Lest you should take your daughters from me by force.’
“ ‘You shall not oppress your neighbor, nor rob him.
You will grope at noonday, as the blind gropes in darkness, and you shall not prosper in your ways. You will only be oppressed and robbed always, and there will be no one to save you.

Your ox will be slain before your eyes, and you will not eat any of it. Your donkey will be violently taken away from before your face, and will not be restored to you. Your sheep will be given to your enemies, and you will have no one to save you.
The men of Shechem set an ambush for him on the tops of the mountains, and they robbed all who came along that way by them; and Abimelech was told about it.

The children of Benjamin did so, and took wives for themselves according to their number, of those who danced, whom they carried off. They went and returned to their inheritance, built the cities, and lived in them.
He killed a huge Egyptian, and the Egyptian had a spear in his hand; but he went down to him with a staff, and plucked the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand, and killed him with his own spear.

He killed an Egyptian, a man of great stature, five cubits* A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters. Therefore this Egyptian was bout 7 feet and 6 inches or 2.28 meters tall. high. In the Egyptian’s hand was a spear like a weaver’s beam; and he went down to him with a staff, plucked the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand, and killed him with his own spear.
For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor.
There are people who remove the landmarks.
There are those who pluck the fatherless from the breast,
Drought and heat consume the snow waters,
All my bones shall say, “Yahweh, who is like you,
For they don’t sleep unless they do evil.
Don’t exploit the poor, because he is poor;
Whoever robs his father or his mother and says, “It’s not wrong,”
to deprive the needy from justice, and to rob the poor among my people of their rights, that widows may be their plunder, and that they may make the fatherless their prey!

definitions.full: H1497. gazal I. גָּזַל verb tear away, seize, rob (Late Hebrew id. , Phoenician גזל Niph`al, Aramaic גְּזַל , & (Nas.) ; Arabic cut off ) — Qal Perfect גָּזַל Job 20:19 ; Ezek 18:18 , גָּזָ֑ל Leviticus 5:23 2 t., גָּזַלְתִּי Psa 69:5 etc.; Imperfect יִגְזֹל Ezek 18:7 , וַיִּגְזֹל 2Sam 23:21 ; 1Chr 11:23 etc.; Infinitive גְּזֹל Isa 10:2 ; Participle active גּוֺזֵל Prov 28:24 ; suffix גֹּזְלוֺ Psa 35:10 ; plural construct גֹּזְלֵי Micah 3:2 ; passive גָּזוּל Deut 28:29 4 t.; — tear away, rob , with object of thing (movable), flock ( עֵדֶר ) Job 24:2 , ass Deut 28:31 , women Judg 21:23 compare Gen 31:31 (E), tear away orphan child from breast Job 24:9 מִשֹּׁד יתום , snatch a spear from enemy's hand 2Sam 23:21 = 1Chr 11:23 ; figurative of drying up snow-water Job 24:19 ; (object stationary) take violent possession of , well of water Gen 21:25 (E), house Job 20:19 , fields Micah 2:2 ; (hyperb.) the skin 3:2 ; with accusative of congnate meaning with verb = seize, plunder , object גְּזֵלָה Leviticus 5:23 (P) Ezek 18:7 , 12 , 16 , גָּזֵל 18:18 ; 22:29 ; indefinite Psa 69:5 ; figurative, object מִשְׁמָּט Isa 10:2 ; with object person robbed Psa 35:10 ; Prov 22:22 ; 28:24 , probably also Judg 9:25 compare Lev 19:13 (H; absolute); compare also passive Deut 28:29 (|| עָשׁוּק ); עושׁק מיד גָּזוּל הציל Jer 21:12 ; compare 22:3 ; Mal 1:13 גָּזוּל (|| מִּסֵּחַ lame and חוֺלֶה sick ), probably that rescued after seizure by wild beasts, therefore mutilated.
